core_obligations: Equivalence of (1) and (3) (proof lines 3042-3045): it was established in the cited lemma on the pro-etale coverings of a w-contractible affine scheme.

(3) implies (2) (proof lines 3047-3061): let F -> G be a surjection of sheaves and let s be a section of G over T; choose a covering over which s lifts to F, refine it by hypothesis to a finite Zariski covering T = the disjoint union of the U_j, note that Zariski coverings are pro-etale coverings so that F(T) is the product of the F(U_j), and conclude that the tuple of local lifts is a section of F over T mapping to s; hence T is weakly contractible.

(2) implies (1) (proof lines 3063-3081): take the faithfully flat weakly etale extension A -> D; the corresponding V = Spec(D) is an object of the big pro-etale site and {V -> T} is a covering, so by subcanonicity the map of representable sheaves h_V -> h_T is surjective; weak contractibility of T produces f in h_V(T) lifting the identity, that is a retraction sigma : D -> A; then for any faithfully flat weakly etale A -> B the base change D -> D tensor_A B has the same properties and admits a retraction, and composing it with sigma yields a retraction of A -> B, so A is w-contractible.
proof_roadmap: Quote the known equivalence of w-contractibility with refinement of pro-etale coverings by finite Zariski coverings.
Deduce weak contractibility by refining a covering and using that sections over a finite Zariski cover are products.
Deduce w-contractibility by turning a faithfully flat weakly etale extension into a covering and using weak contractibility to produce the retraction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of w-contractibility of an affine ring A, weak contractibility of the corresponding object of the big pro-etale site and the refinement property for pro-etale coverings by finite Zariski coverings (statement lines 3026-3040). The proof (proof lines 3042-3084) quotes the known equivalence of the first and third conditions, deduces weak contractibility by refining coverings and using products over finite Zariski covers, and deduces w-contractibility by producing a retraction from a faithfully flat weakly etale extension. H2: two implications with four inputs, written out in full.
